info.title: Bunkarr API
info.description: Bunkarr REST API. Authenticate with the API key from Settings > General in the X-Api-Key header (or the apikey query parameter), or with a login session cookie. The *arr webhook routes (/webhook/...) accept only an integration's webhook key instead. Errors are {"message": "..."}: 400 invalid input, 401 not authenticated, 403 refused (a cross-site browser request, an action that needs a login session, a directory Bunkarr cannot read), 404 unknown id, 409 conflict with the current state (including safety refusals that need a confirmation or a mounted share), 429 too many requests (Retry-After), 502 Plex, plex.tv or an *arr failed, 503 unavailable (the backup routes of a server without backup services, or a request stopped as the server shuts down), 500 anything else. Secrets (Plex tokens, *arr API keys, Apprise URLs) are write-only; a webhook key appears only in POST /integrations/{id}/webhook/key. Job-starting endpoints answer 202 with the queued Job. Sizes are bytes, times RFC 3339.

Capabilities.description: What the destination probe found (design section 3).

unstableInodes.description: Inode numbers do not tell whether two names at the destination are one file: a hardlinked name (or another spelling on a case-insensitive destination) stats with other numbers than the name it is one file with, as on a CIFS mount with noserverino. Bunkarr then compares such names by content. A sync, verify or retention job that is not a dry run checks this again before it first compares two names and stores a change.

probeVersion.description: Version of the probe that found these capabilities (currently 1). 0 or missing: an older probe that did not check unstableInodes; the next sync, verify or retention job that is not a dry run probes the destination again, and until then inode numbers are not trusted.

enforcesModes.description: The destination keeps a file's permission bits (the probe writes a file with mode 0600 and reads the mode back; SMB without POSIX extensions does not). *arr backups need it unless their integration sets backup.acceptInsecureModes. Missing or false until a probe that checks it.
